formal_sketch.consequent: For each i in 0..NumAlerts-1, an instance of prim_alert_sender is generated with parameters AsyncOn set to AlertAsyncOn[i] and IsFatal set to IsFatal[i]

guarantees.claim: Each instance connects alert_req_i to alert[i], alert_rx_i to alert_rx_i[i], alert_tx_o to alert_tx_o[i]; alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are left unconnected.

assumptions.claim: Alert inputs alert[i] and alert_rx_i[i] are driven by external logic according to the prim_alert_sender protocol (valid handshake or level timing).
assumptions.risk: If the protocol is violated (e.g., missing pulses, out of sequence), the alert sender may not propagate alerts correctly, causing missed or false alerts.

uncertain_points.claim: prim_alert_sender output ports alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are left unconnected; it is unknown whether the module requires these ports to be driven/monitored for correct alert handling (e.g., handshake completion, fault state reporting).
uncertain_points.cond: When an alert is active or under test
uncertain_points.risk: If the sender expects an acknowledge handshake on alert_ack_o, leaving it open may stall the alert state machine, causing a persistent alert, deadlock, or loss of subsequent alerts. Missing state feedback may hide fault conditions.

formal_sketch.antecedent: When an alert is active or under test
formal_sketch.consequent: prim_alert_sender output ports alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are left unconnected; it is unknown whether the module requires these ports to be driven/monitored for correct alert handling (e.g., handshake completion, fault state reporting)

security_implications: Unconnected alert_ack_o and alert_state_o on the alert sender may impair alert handling; if the module expects an external acknowledgment or state feedback to reset the alert, open ports could cause an alert to be latched indefinitely (denial of service) or prevent detection of subsequent alerts (loss of security events). This is a high-severity fault containment gap in the security alert infrastructure.
